en.title: Subset with the Fewest Elements and a Larger Sum
en.description:
Split the array by element positions into A and B, keeping duplicate values. It is required that sum(A)>sum(B); first minimize the number of elements in A, then maximize the sum of A for that count, and return A in ascending order. B may be empty.

The input/output protocol was compiled by this site, and missing numeric constraints are explicitly marked as this site's additions.
en.input: The first line contains n, and the second line contains the array. Full original bounds: 1≤n≤100000, 1≤arr[i]≤100000.
en.output: Output the number of elements in A on the first line, followed by one integer per line in non-decreasing order, keeping duplicates.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 2 / 4 / 5; 2 / 5 / 6; 2 / 1 / 1. These answers were verified by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Sort the elements in descending order and take the largest remaining element one at a time; stop the first time the sum taken is strictly greater than the remaining sum, and output the taken prefix in reverse.
